open-question.question: The commit tool repeats every git write that exits 128, up to 16 attempts over about four seconds, reading only the exit status and never git's message, so a failure no lock caused, such as a pathspec matching no file, is repeated to the last attempt before its error prints. Does the tool keep repeating every exit 128, or does it stop at once on one no lock caused, which needs it to read git's message text or to tell the two cases apart some other way?
open-question.recommendation: No lock is ever missed over git's wording or locale, and the cost is about four seconds before a failure that ends the call anyway, with git's own message still printed whole.
open-question.alternative: The commit tool keeps repeating every git write that exits 128 on the present schedule (16 attempts, 0.25 seconds apart), reading only the exit status and no message text. A failure no lock caused, such as `git add` of a pathspec matching no file, is still repeated to the last attempt before its `Error:` line prints. The committing invariant stays as written, and CLAUDE.md records the entry as accepted with its reason. Nothing changes in the tool, its tests, or the committing invariant, and no lock is ever missed because of git's wording, its locale, or a new lock message: the only cost is about four seconds before a failure that ends the call anyway, and git's own message still reaches the runner whole. Every non-lock 128 costs about four seconds and reports itself as "on all 16 attempts", which reads as a held lock and can send a runner to look for one; how often this happens depends on how the sibling question on committing a removed path settles, since that case is the one reproduced.

The tool keeps repeating every exit 128 without reading any message, but its one schedule constant is cut to a smaller window (for example a handful of attempts over about one second), so a non-lock failure surfaces sooner; nothing tells the two kinds of failure apart. The change is two constants and the retry test's bounds, with no message parsing and no new branch, and it shrinks the wasted wait on every non-lock failure in proportion. It narrows the window that absorbs another run's ordinary write, the reason the retry exists, below the bounds `tests/test_commit_retry.py` pins as decided, so concurrent runs (two completion runs, a sweep beside a completion run) collide more often; and a non-lock failure is still repeated and still reported as a multi-attempt failure.

After a write exits 128, the tool reads git's stderr and repeats the write only when it holds git's lock-file text (the `Unable to create '….lock': File exists` form that a held index, `HEAD`, or ref lock prints); every other exit 128 is passed on at once as one `Error:` line after its single attempt. Git is run with a fixed C locale so the message is not translated. The committing invariant's "no message text is read" is revised and the retry tests gain a non-lock 128 that fails on the first attempt. It stops exactly the failures that are not locks, whatever their cause, so a pathspec, repository, or permission failure is reported at once and honestly as one attempt, while every lock git reports in its standard form is still absorbed. The tool depends on git's message wording: a git version that rewords the lock message, or a lock failure printed in another form, is no longer retried and collides at once, the failure the retry was built to prevent; the fixed locale must cover every git write the tool runs.

After a write exits 128, the tool reads git's stderr and stops at once only when it matches a short stated list of failures no lock causes (starting with `pathspec '…' did not match any files`); every other exit 128, an unrecognized message included, is repeated on the present schedule. Git runs under a fixed C locale; the committing invariant is revised to name the list. A wording change in git or an unlisted message falls back to today's behaviour, so no lock is ever left unretried; the reproduced case and any later one found in the field stop at once. It closes only the failures someone has listed, so each new non-lock 128 still waits the full window until it is added, and the list is message-matching code the tool must keep current with git; if the sibling question on removed paths stops the pathspec case from reaching git, the list may hold nothing that occurs.

After a write exits 128, the tool reads no message text but checks git's own lock files, resolved through `git rev-parse --git-path` (the index lock, `HEAD.lock`, and the current branch's ref lock): it repeats the write while one of them exists, repeats it once more when none exists so a lock released between the failure and the probe is still absorbed, and passes on a further 128 with no lock file present after that second attempt. It tells a lock from a non-lock by the lock itself rather than by git's wording or locale, so the invariant's "no message text is read" can stand, and a non-lock failure ends after two attempts instead of sixteen. The tool gains file probes and a branch on what git keeps under its directory, a lock it does not probe (another ref, a packed-refs or config lock) is treated as a non-lock after two attempts, and the retry test must hold each probed lock file, so the mechanics grow more than a message match would.
